samples.summary: Feature is unreachable on the shipped dependency pin — the design's Goals are unmet by this PR
samples.evidence: `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` gates `supportsClientKey()`, and every surface is behind it: `useDurableDocument` refuses eligibility, the Settings `Offline` section is not rendered (`app/settings/page.tsx`), and the chip's offer is suppressed. `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` and this diff does not bump it, so `supportsClientKey()` is false in every production build. The design's Goals ("Edits made while disconnected survive a reload… on a device where the user has asked for it") therefore hold for nobody: no user can opt in, no document is ever durable, and the new chip state is unreachable outside tests. The design doc does state this is intentional ("PR 4 lands inert… the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), so this may be an accepted trade — but as shipped the outcome does not work for a user, and the dependency bump is the only thing that makes any of this code run.

samples.summary: Near-verbatim clone of `date-format-preference.ts` instead of a shared preference helper; the two copies have already diverged
samples.evidence: `offline-persistence-preference.ts` duplicates `lib/date-format-preference.ts` line for line — same `STORAGE_KEY`/`CHANGE_EVENT` pair, same `memoryEnabled`/`memoryFormat` session mirror, same `useSyncExternalStore` wrapper, even the same explanatory comments ("Session-only copy of the preference, set *only* when persisting it failed…"). The design says only that it is "built on `lib/date-format-preference.ts`'s shape", which a shared `createLocalPreference(key, parse, default)` factory would satisfy with one implementation. They have already diverged in one behavior: the new module retires the stale mirror on a cross-tab `storage` event (module-scope listener), while `date-format-preference.ts` does not — so the same bug is fixed in one copy and live in the other, and any future fix must be made twice.

samples.summary: The "last segment of an SDK store key" rule is written three times in one PR, against the PR's own warning
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` exports `documentKeyOf(key)` and its doc comment says it lives there "because this module is where store keys are consumed, and two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false". The same PR then adds a second copy in `offline-copy.ts` (`documentIdOf`: `docKey.split("/"); parts[parts.length - 1] || docKey`) and a third inline in `offline-copy-recovery.ts` `describeArchivedDocument` (`const parts = docKey.split("/"); const key = parts[parts.length - 1] || docKey;`). `documentKeyOf` is exported and importable from both. This is exactly the divergence the store's own comment says previously produced a silently-false guard.

samples.summary: Design doc states archives stay user-scoped in the 30-day sweep; the implementation sweeps every account's archives
samples.evidence: The doc says of the periodic sweep: "Archives stay scoped: another account's is the only copy of work their SDK could not reconcile, and it is theirs to collect." `WafflebaseDocStore.collectStale` calls `this.dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` with no `onlyUser` argument (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1190), and its own comment states the opposite ("Archives are swept on exactly the same terms… across every account on this device"), with a test asserting it (`collects another account's stale entries and their stale archives`). The `onlyUser` parameter on `dropArchivesWhere` is consequently never passed by any caller. One of the two has to be corrected; as filed the canonical doc describes behavior the code does not have.

samples.summary: Design doc names the wrong existing engine for offline-copy recovery (`DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`)
samples.evidence: The doc says "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`" and lists document-copy.md in See Also as "the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". The implementation reuses neither: `offline-copy-recovery.ts` calls `createDocument()` then `applyImportedContent()` (the *import* engine) for sheet/doc/slides/board, and for notes hand-rolls a `new Client()` + attach + `root.content = new Text()` in `writeNote` because `applyImportedContent` has no note branch. The chosen path is arguably the correct one (the copy endpoint copies from a server-side source document, which does not exist here), so the doc — not the code — is what is wrong; but a reader routed to `document-copy.md` will not find the machinery this path uses. The bespoke `writeNote` also duplicates `applyImportedContent`'s client lifecycle rather than adding a `note` arm to it.

samples.summary: Housekeeping runs for every signed-in user regardless of the opt-in or the capability gate, contradicting "users who never opt in pay nothing"
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute` mounts `<OfflineRuntime userId={...} />` unconditionally, and its effect reads neither `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` nor `supportsClientKey()`. Every signed-in session therefore opens an IndexedDB connection (`new WafflebaseDocStore`), runs `retryPendingOfflineErase()`, runs the thirty-day `collectStale()`, and issues an extra `fetchDocuments()` (`GET /documents`, outside react-query so not deduped with the documents page) to drive `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. The design states the opposite property: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing." On the shipped pin nobody *can* opt in, so this is per-session cost for a feature that is inert for 100% of users. A `supportsClientKey()`/preference guard, or short-circuiting when `storedDocumentIds()` is empty, would keep the promise.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` issues two extra network requests before every delete, ungated — unlike `removeMember`, which does gate
samples.evidence: `deleteWorkspace` calls `documentIdsIn(id)` unconditionally, which performs `fetchWorkspace(ref)` plus a full `fetchDocuments()` listing before the DELETE, for every user on every workspace deletion — including users who never enabled offline saving and builds where `supportsClientKey()` is false. `removeMember` two functions below does gate the identical call (`const leaving = isOfflineUser(String(userId)); const doomed = leaving ? await documentIdsIn(workspaceId) : [];`), so the asymmetry looks unintended. It also weakens an existing assertion: `api/url.test.ts` had to relax "every request URL contains the encoded id" to "some request URL does" precisely because of this companion listing.

samples.summary: Recovery notification does not name which of the three loss reasons applied, as the design requires
samples.evidence: The design's Losing work anyway section says "The user is then told what happened, in the vocabulary of the three reasons" (`epoch-reanchor`, `document-purged`, `actor-mismatch`). The implementation's toast is generic: `Edits to "${title}" could not be reconciled with the server. They are still on this device.` The reason is available at latch time (`DurableLossWatch` receives the `local-changes-dropped` event, whose payload carries `reason`) but is discarded — `expectLoss(docKey)` takes no reason and `ArchiveRecord` has no field for one, so it cannot be recovered later. Relatedly, the design says the offline-transition toast "changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'"; in `sync-status-chip.tsx` the toast only fires while `stranded`, so on a durable document no toast appears at all (defensible, but not what the doc states).
searchedFor: grep 'expectLoss' in wafflebase-doc-store.ts and ArchiveRecord fields

samples.summary: Design doc's store-migration paragraph describes an `onupgradeneeded` relocation the implementation deliberately does not do
samples.evidence: The doc says "An `onupgradeneeded` that relocates each existing value into the snapshot store, with an empty change log beside it, is the whole migration." `WafflebaseDocStore.open()` ships `DB_VERSION = 1` with a create-only upgrade path, and its comment states the reasoning the doc omits: "Version 1 creates; there is nothing in the wild to migrate. No wafflebase build has ever passed `ClientOptions.store`, so no browser holds an older layout." The code's reasoning is right; the doc describes a migration that does not exist and would mislead the next person changing the schema.

samples.summary: `frontend.md` still describes `PrivateRoute`'s `YorkieProvider` as the Yorkie client connection, unchanged by the per-document move
samples.evidence: `frontend.md:56-57` ("**PrivateRoute** — … Wraps children in `YorkieProvider`") and the tree at :73-74 ("PrivateRoute └── YorkieProvider (Yorkie client connection)") are the canonical description of the frontend's Yorkie architecture. This change nests a second, per-document `YorkieProvider` inside `CollabDocumentProvider` and mounts a new `OfflineRuntime` under `PrivateRoute`; neither appears in `frontend.md`, and the new doc's own See Also names `frontend.md` as "the Yorkie client and presence architecture this moves from per-session to per-document". A cross-reference line in the canonical subsystem doc would keep it accurate without duplicating the new document.
searchedFor: git diff of docs/design/ in this change (only README, sync-status, new doc touched)

samples.summary: The Rollout table's PR split is not followed — PRs 2, 3, 4 and 5 land as one change
samples.evidence: The Rollout section states "The structural change and the behavior change land separately, so that a regression in either is unambiguous" and enumerates PR 2 (store, not wired), PR 3 (per-document client, still no store), PR 4 (wire the store + opt-in + chip + recovery), PR 5 (revise `sync-status.md`). This diff contains all four. The inertness of `supportsClientKey()` bounds the blast radius, so the risk the split was protecting against is largely covered by other means — but the doc as written no longer describes how the work actually shipped.

samples.summary: An upstream test suite is transcribed into `src/` as a non-test module, and the design doc does not record it
samples.evidence: `doc-store-contract.ts` is a verbatim copy of the SDK's `packages/sdk/test/unit/client/doc_store_contract.ts` at v0.7.22, living under `src/lib/` (not `*.test.ts`) and importing `vitest` at module scope. The file justifies the copy well (the SDK publishes only `dist`, and the copy is run against `MemoryDocStore` so drift fails in CI), but vendoring upstream test code is the kind of decision the design doc should record — it is absent from `offline-local-persistence.md`, and the next SDK bump needs a human to re-transcribe it.

finding.summary: Feature is unreachable on the shipped dependency pin — the design's Goals are unmet by this PR
finding.evidence: `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` gates `supportsClientKey()`, and every surface is behind it: `useDurableDocument` refuses eligibility, the Settings `Offline` section is not rendered (`app/settings/page.tsx`), and the chip's offer is suppressed. `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` and this diff does not bump it, so `supportsClientKey()` is false in every production build. The design's Goals ("Edits made while disconnected survive a reload… on a device where the user has asked for it") therefore hold for nobody: no user can opt in, no document is ever durable, and the new chip state is unreachable outside tests. The design doc does state this is intentional ("PR 4 lands inert… the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), so this may be an accepted trade — but as shipped the outcome does not work for a user, and the dependency bump is the only thing that makes any of this code run.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real and verified: MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23" (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:24), supportsClientKey() reads the pin injected by vite.config.ts:414-418, and packages/frontend/package.json:66 pins "@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22", so the gate is closed in every production build and all four surfaces (use-durable-document.ts:128, app/settings/page.tsx:35, sync-status-chip.tsx:85, collab-document-provider.tsx:223) are inert. But under the design-fit / spec-conformance rubric this is not a blocking mismatch: the canonical design doc specifies exactly this state as the intended rollout. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:539-549 states "PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release… supportsClientKey() gates both opt-in entry points on @yorkie-js/react >= 0.7.23, and at the time of writing npm's newest is 0.7.22… the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped. Bumping it is the whole remaining action — no code here changes with it." Lines 209-213 of the same doc positively require both opt-in entry points to be gated on supportsClientKey(), so the diff conforms; not gating them would have been the violation. The plan document repeats it (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:38-41, :220, :243-246). The enabling release (yorkie-js-sdk#1357 / 0.7.23) is recorded as unpublished, so the demanded bump was not an available action for this diff, and the preference ships off by default (design doc :524-526) so nothing regresses for any user — only a deferred benefit, tracked in the active task doc. That makes this a documented, deliberate rollout state rather than an unmet acceptance criterion; at most a minor tracking point, which does not block.
